facts.text: Cost estimating and schedule guides are published handbooks for building auditable cost estimates and project schedules, written by the United States Government Accountability Office (GAO) and AACE International, a professional association for cost engineering.
facts.quote: These are published handbooks on how to build a cost estimate and a project schedule that can withstand audit, written by the United States Government Accountability Office (GAO) and by AACE International, a professional association for cost engineering.

facts.text: GAO audits government programs and has distilled the characteristics of a defensible estimate.
facts.quote: GAO audits government programs and has distilled what a defensible estimate looks like.

facts.text: GAO's Schedule Assessment Guide (GAO-16-89G, December 2015) sets out ten best-practice areas for a reliable integrated schedule, including capturing all activities, sequencing activities with logic, resourcing activities, and performing schedule-risk analysis.
facts.quote: Its Schedule Assessment Guide (GAO-16-89G, December 2015) sets out ten best-practice areas for a reliable integrated schedule, including that all activities are captured, sequenced with logic, resourced, and that a schedule-risk analysis is performed.

facts.text: GAO's Cost Estimating and Assessment Guide (GAO-20-195G, March 2020) is the cost companion to the Schedule Assessment Guide.

facts.text: AACE International's Recommended Practice 57R-09 describes integrated cost and schedule risk analysis using risk drivers and Monte Carlo simulation of a critical-path model.
